phases.title: Combat
phases.summary: Melee is done end to end and verified by a headless gate. Spells cast and deal damage; auras do not exist yet.

items.text: RollMeleeOutcomeAgainst — one urand(0, 10000) against a running sum
items.note: In the order miss, dodge, parry, block, glancing, crushing, crit, normal. Reproduced structurally, including the (tmp -= skillBonus) > 0 mutation inside the branch conditions.

items.text: The roll is inclusive at both ends, so there are 10001 outcomes and not 10000
Facing asymmetry: only a player victim loses its dodge from behind
items.note: Parry and block are lost by anyone. That is what makes tanking a boss survivable, not an oversight.

items.text: creature_template.flags_extra vendored and wired — the five bits that gate table branches
items.note: NoDodge, NoParry, NoBlock, NoCrushingBlows, NoCrit. 4/4/5/1/4 creatures carry them.

items.text: Distribution verified over 10⁶ rolls, within 0.05 % of the chances asked for
CalcArmorReducedDamage — the x/(1+x) curve, the level-59 kink, the 75 % cap
items.note: And the ceil that stops heavy armour making a target immune to weak hits.

items.text: Outcome multipliers: crit ×2, crushing +½ (integer, truncated), glancing −10 %/level capped at three, flat block
items.note: Dodge and parry preserve clean damage for rage and threat.

items.text: ARMOUR IS APPLIED BEFORE THE OUTCOME MULTIPLIER, not after
items.note: Observably different on about half of all inputs because of the ceil between them.

items.text: MeleeChances — the miss curve's two asymmetries, boss dodge/parry, humanoid-only parry
items.note: 0.04 vs 0.02 against a player; a cliff at ten points against a creature.

items.text: Percentages become hundredths as int32(chance × 100) in FLOAT, not double
items.note: 13.4f × 100 rounds to exactly 1340.0f, so a boss's parry is 1340 where decimal arithmetic says 1339.

items.text: SMSG_ATTACKERSTATEUPDATE, whose trailers are conditional on HitInfo
items.note: An extra or missing one shifts every byte after it and the client notices several packets later.

items.text: Overkill is measured against the victim's health BEFORE the hit
items.note: Upstream sends the packet and only then applies the damage.

items.text: SMSG_ATTACKSTART sends full guids where SMSG_ATTACKSTOP packs them
items.note: Upstream's inconsistency, reproduced rather than tidied.

items.text: CMSG_ATTACKSWING / CMSG_ATTACKSTOP, and every rejection answers with a stop rather than silence
Swing timers: a timer overshoots into the negative for exactly one tick
items.note: min(timer + speed, speed) carries that overshoot into the next swing rather than discarding it.

items.text: A failed swing costs a 100 ms retry, not a weapon swing
Swing errors are suppressed to one per run of failures
items.note: The flip side: a fight that is out of range throughout emits exactly one packet, which makes a persistent failure look silent.

items.text: Kill lands on Corpse, never on JustDied — upstream promotes through it in one call
Corpse delay from rank (60 s common, 300 s rare/elite, 600 s open-world boss)
THE RESPAWN CLOCK INCLUDES THE CORPSE DELAY
items.note: Measuring from the corpse's removal instead would bring everything back a minute early.

items.text: A despawned creature leaves its cell and the guid index but stays in the update list
Threat: one point per point of damage; zero threat still joins the list
THE VICTIM IS STICKY: 110 % to steal it in melee range, 130 % out of it
items.note: Without the margin a creature thrashes between two similar attackers and tanking cannot work. Measured: 1 switch over 100 alternating swings.

items.text: Aggro radius: 20 yards at parity, ±1/level, clamped to 5–45
items.note: Upstream's GetAggroRange has its two locals named backwards — the one called creatureLevel holds the target's level — so this follows GetAttackDistance, which computes the same thing with honest names.

items.text: A missing faction template is treated as HARMLESS
items.note: The safe direction to fail — a creature that never fights is noticed; a zone that attacks on sight reads as a game rule.

items.text: Leash at 30 yards from the SPAWN POINT, not from where the fight started
Evading clears the threat list, not only the victim
A creature turns to face its victim
items.note: Not cosmetic: the swing loop enforces a 120° cone, so a creature that never turns stands next to its victim and never lands a hit.

items.text: Spell.dbc — 49,839 rows, 234 columns — plus the four tables it indexes into
items.note: Cast time, range and duration are indices, not values.

items.text: BASEPOINTS IS STORED ONE BELOW THE MINIMUM
items.note: Fireball's 14-22 is base 13 with 9 sides; reading the column as the minimum makes every spell in the game hit for one less.

items.text: Costs come from two columns
items.note: Wrath moved caster spells to a percentage of base mana and left rage and energy flat, so reading only ManaCost finds every mage spell free.

items.text: Effects are three PARALLEL BLOCKS, not three interleaved records
CMSG_CAST_SPELL and its target block, whose layout is decided by a leading mask
items.note: Five separate flags share ONE guid field, not one each.

items.text: SMSG_SPELL_START and SMSG_SPELL_GO — two packets per cast, not one
THE CASTER GUID IS WRITTEN TWICE in each
items.note: The first is whatever produced the cast, the second is always the unit; writing it once shifts every field after it by a guid.

items.text: SMSG_SPELL_GO's hit and miss lists use FULL guids where the rest of the packet packs them
items.note: And the two lists have different strides — a miss carries a reason byte, a hit does not.

items.text: THE GLOBAL COOLDOWN BLOCKS ONLY SPELLS THAT WOULD START ONE
items.note: An ability with no StartRecoveryTime — Heroic Strike, say — is usable during it.

items.text: Power is taken when the cast STARTS, not when it lands, so a cancelled cast is not free
POWER SLOTS ARE INDEXED BY TYPE
items.note: Power used to always read slot 0, so a warrior's rage went into the mana field — a full mana bar and an empty rage bar on the same unit.

items.text: A SINGLE DIE SIDE ADDS EXACTLY 1 AND DRAWS NO RANDOM NUMBER
items.note: Upstream has an explicit case 1; folding it into irand(1, 1) gives the same answer and desynchronises the stream.

items.text: SCHOOL_DAMAGE, HEAL, and the three weapon-damage forms — 4 of upstream's 164
A WEAPON-DAMAGE EFFECT'S VALUE IS A FLAT BONUS ON TOP OF A SWING
items.note: Treating it as damage makes Heroic Strike hit for 11 instead of a swing plus 11.

items.text: Armour is applied ONCE AT THE END, not per effect
items.note: It ceilings, so per-effect mitigation gains a point per effect.

items.text: SMSG_SPELLNONMELEEDAMAGELOG — THE TARGET IS WRITTEN BEFORE THE CASTER
items.note: The opposite order to SMSG_ATTACKERSTATEUPDATE, with nothing in either packet saying so.

items.text: player_xp_for_level vendored — 79 rows. EACH ROW IS THE COST OF LEAVING THAT LEVEL
items.note: Not a running total; reading it as a total makes every level after the first cost far too much.

items.text: Acore::XP::BaseGain — two different curves either side of the player's level
GetGrayLevel (three segments, flat floor under 6) and GetZeroDifference (a nine-step widening function)
items.note: Neither derivable from the other.

items.text: The base figure comes from the CONTENT, not the creature's level: 45 classic, 235 Outland, 580 Northrend
Elite pays double — and RARE IS NOT ELITE, despite ranking above world boss numerically
Critters and anything flagged NoExperience pay nothing
items.note: Or a field of rabbits is a levelling strategy.

items.text: GiveXP as a LOOP, with the surplus carried forward — one kill can cross several levels
Level-up recomputes health, mana and the five attributes, and REFILLS health and mana
SMSG_LOG_XPGAIN, whose LAYOUT DEPENDS ON WHETHER THERE WAS A VICTIM
SMSG_LEVELUP_INFO, which carries DELTAS RATHER THAN TOTALS, in fixed-size arrays
Experience is paid BEFORE the threat list is cleared
items.note: Creature.Kill forgets everyone, so paying afterwards pays nobody and looks like a kill that simply awards nothing.

items.text: tools/harness/m5_combat.py — an M5 gate driving the whole loop over the real protocol
items.note: Log in, walk to a wolf, auto-attack, kill it, gain experience. Measured: ~9 swings each way, 50 experience for a level 1 kill. Passes repeatedly.

items.text: A PLAYER HAD NO WEAPON DAMAGE AND NO ATTACK TIME
items.note: Both are update fields defaulting to zero, so an unequipped character swung every tick for nothing, with no error anywhere — M5 was literally unreachable. Found by writing the gate, not by any unit test.

items.text: Verify against a real 3.3.5a client
items.note: The gate proves the server's packets are self-consistent and carry the right numbers; it cannot prove the client reads them the same way. Only a real client can answer that.

phases.title: Progression systems
phases.summary: Inventory, loot, quests, vendors, trainers, gossip, talents, reputation, corpses, chat, commands. Player death is done — it was the hole creatures fighting back opened.

items.text: Player death lands on Corpse, the same promotion a creature makes — JustDied is the moment things that happen once happen, not a state anything updates in
THE THREE STATES ARE NOT TWO: alive, a corpse that cannot move, and a ghost that can
items.note: The client keys movement off the health value, so a ghost gets 1 point and not 0. Leave it at zero after release and the player is stuck on the spot with the release button gone.

items.text: A creature that kills a player forgets it and goes home
items.note: Without this it stands over the corpse swinging at something the swing loop refuses to hit, forever — the player never releases, so nothing ever clears the threat list.

items.text: The corpse position is remembered at release, which is what a corpse run walks back to
CMSG_REPOP_REQUEST releases to the nearest usable graveyard; CMSG_RECLAIM_CORPSE resurrects at the body
Resurrecting restores half health and mana, and EMPTIES RAGE rather than halving it
items.note: Rage is earned in combat. Half a bar you did not fight for is a different resource.

items.text: game_graveyard_zone vendored (700 links across 163 zones); coordinates come from WorldSafeLocs.dbc
items.note: Newer AzerothCore reads them from a game_graveyard table the vendored dump predates. The same divergence as creature_template_model — the data is what this follows. Measured: a human dying at the Northshire start releases 58 yards away, to 'Elwynn Forest, Northshire'.

items.text: The faction filter runs before the distance comparison
items.note: 570 of the 700 rows are neutral, so forgetting it looks like it works — until a contested zone leaves a player with nowhere to go.

items.text: A graveyard on another map is skipped, and a zone with none leaves the ghost where it fell
items.note: There is no cross-map transfer yet. Releasing somewhere unreachable is worse than not moving; standing over your own corpse, you can still reclaim.

items.text: Resurrection sickness, and the spirit healer's own resurrect
A real Corpse object — the body is currently a remembered position rather than something other players can see
The corpse reclaim delay is sent but never enforced; reclaiming is allowed immediately
Inventory and items
Loot (*_loot_template)
Quests — accept, objective, complete, reward

phases.title: The tick
phases.summary: The threading model PLAN §4.2 calls the single most important constraint in the port.

items.text: Outbound packets go through a Channel with one writer task
items.note: Sending never touches a socket, so gameplay code on a map worker cannot block behind a slow client.

items.text: Header encryption begins at a POSITION IN THE SEND QUEUE, not a moment in time
items.note: Otherwise the plaintext challenge would be encrypted if the writer had not caught up.

items.text: Map is synchronous and lock-free; safety comes from the tick's ordering, not a mutex
World loop: drain the scheduler → drain sessions → run maps, in that order and never overlapping
MapUpdater — dedicated threads, not the thread pool, so a callback storm cannot starve a tick
One inbound queue per session, drained by whichever loop may run the packet at its front
items.note: The two-queue design in PLAN §4.2 was withdrawn: the M3 gate caught a character saving at its pre-movement position because logout overtook movement. Upstream's head-of-line blocking is what makes it correct.

items.text: Handlers resume on the loop that started them
items.note: ConfigureAwait(true) under the tick's SynchronizationContext, so a database answer never lands on a pool thread holding a Player.

items.text: Per-viewer update batching — one SMSG_UPDATE_OBJECT per tick instead of one per object
items.note: Logging in at Northshire went from 131 packets to 1.

items.text: Analyzer banning bare Task.Run in gameplay code
AssertOwnerThread is not called anywhere yet
items.note: The invariant is documented and structural, but nothing fails loudly if a future caller breaks it.

items.text: Map workers default to 0 (inline). The pool is written and tested but unproven under load.
GRID LOADING BLOCKS THE TICK IT HAPPENS ON
items.note: Measured: 875 ticks/second idle, but the tick a player logs in on takes ~71 ms, over the 50 ms budget, because the grid around them builds ~960 creatures inside the map update. Upstream splits this per cell rather than per grid.

items: Bans and suspensions — FailBanned / FailSuspended exist as codes but nothing ever sends them; there is no account_banned table and no IP ban list
Failed-login lockout — passwords can be guessed at socket speed
Realm flags are static — a realm shows as online whether or not the world server is running
Realm population is always 0, and the character count per realm is always 0
CMSG_TIME_SYNC_RESP is never handled — the request is sent once and the reply ignored, so the server has no clock offset for the client
Latency is never measured, despite answering every ping
Account data (CMSG_UPDATE_ACCOUNT_DATA) is never stored, so client-side settings do not follow the account
Tutorial flags are always zero and never saved
MOTD comes from config, not from a database table
Banned-addon list is always empty; client cache version is a static config value
Logout is instant — upstream makes a player sit for 20 seconds unless resting or a GM
SessionStatus.Transfer is never entered; nothing moves between maps yet

Per-observer field filtering — UpdateMask.IntersectWith exists but nothing computes which fields a given observer may see, so every observer currently gets every non-zero field. A real information leak once there is anything private to leak.
Create-block branches for Transport, HasTarget and Vehicle are unwritten. Living, StationaryPosition, Self, Position, LowGuid and Rotation are all produced.
Our deflate output is not byte-identical to upstream's, by design (PLAN §9 excludes compressed bodies from byte-exact comparison)
Only position, zone, map and orientation are saved — level, health and stats are recomputed from base tables on every login, so any change to them is lost
No name profanity or reserved-name checks
No declined names (the Russian client asks for them)
Character deletion is immediate — no in-progress state, no undelete window

There is no real Corpse object. A dead player's body is a remembered position, not something another player can see or walk up to — and the reclaim delay is sent to the client but never enforced, so reclaiming is allowed immediately.
LOOT DOES NOT EXIST, so UNIT_DYNFLAG_LOOTABLE is deliberately never set on a corpse — the flag would promise a lootable corpse that opens an empty window.
creature_addon is not vendored, so every creature is ReactState.Aggressive. A passive quest prop currently behaves like anything else and will fight back.
A creature's facing is server-side only. CreatureAi.FaceTowards decides whether a swing lands, but the client is not told — that needs the facing-target form of SMSG_MONSTER_MOVE.
Glancing blows exclude a pet victim upstream; pets do not exist here, so only the player half of that condition is modelled.
Threat has no taunt, no redirection and no aura modifiers, and MeleeChances has no aura or expertise terms.
Nothing checks that a player knows the spell it casts. There is no spellbook, so CMSG_CAST_SPELL is honoured for any id in Spell.dbc.
SPELLS CANNOT MISS, CRIT OR BE RESISTED. Every cast that passes its checks lands in full — no spell hit table, no spell crit, no resistance.
AURAS DO NOT EXIST, so APPLY_AURA — the single most common effect in the file — does nothing. Fireball's direct damage lands; its burn does not.
A creature's spell damage is not rescaled by its level. Upstream multiplies by the ratio of the creature's base damage to the spell's for spells flagged to scale.
Nothing interrupts a cast. Moving, taking damage and dying all leave the bar running; only CMSG_CANCEL_CAST ends one early.

Experience is paid in full to everyone on the threat list, not split. Group splitting needs groups; paying each participant the whole amount errs towards over-rewarding, which is visible, rather than silently paying nobody.
The content level comes from the creature's template expansion, not its zone. Upstream uses the zone, so a classic creature standing in Outland pays classic rates here and Outland rates there.
There is no rested experience, no recruit-a-friend and no group rate. All three are multipliers on top of a figure that is computed correctly.
They do nothing. No opening, looting, using, or trapping — a gameobject stands where its row puts it and can be looked at.
The 32 data0..data31 columns are not read, so nothing knows what a door opens with or where a teleporter goes
gameobject_template_addon is not read, so per-spawn faction and flag overrides are missing
Three templates carry size = 0 and 11 spawns use them; they are drawn at nothing. Upstream does the same, so it is reproduced rather than corrected — but it looks like a bug when found.
1,193 spawns have no display id. These are invisible triggers and upstream creates them too, but each still costs a create block to a client that will never see anything.
Rotation is computed once at spawn and is not an update field
Movement ignores collision entirely — a creature walks through walls, trees and each other, because there is no pathfinding yet

Health uses no per-rank rate. Upstream multiplies by Rate.Creature.*.HP from the config; all five default to 1.0 and there is no config system for them, so they are omitted rather than hard-coded to a number that would look deliberate.
creature_addon and creature_equip_template are not read, so no creature has visible weapons or its spawn auras

The damage formula follows our DATA, not the C++ checkout: the current tree scales damage_base by a BaseVariance column our dump predates, so the older mindmg/maxdmg/dmg_multiplier form is used instead.
No aura or item contributes to damage, because neither exists — upstream runs the result through four modifier layers that are all identity without them
Difficulty entries (difficulty_entry_1..3) are ignored; every creature is built from its normal-mode template
phaseMask is loaded and stored but never checked — everything is visible to everyone

Links are not read from .mmtile and must not be — the file reserves MaxLinkCount links' worth of space, but Detour builds them when a tile is added, so what is on disk is uninitialised. Anything that starts reading them is reading noise.

The under-the-world threshold (25 yards) is a judgement, not a measurement. It has been exercised by the gate walking on open ground, not by a real client in a city or a cave — the false-positive rate is unknown.
Vmap tiles are loaded on demand and never unloaded, the same gap grid loading has.
CollectCandidates allocates a List<uint> per group per ray. Fine for the tests, not for a tick.
The single-child (BVH2) branch of the BIH walk is written from the C++ and never observed firing in a test.

132 of 436 sampled model groups carry an all-zero bounding box while holding real geometry. A zero box means "not recorded", not "empty" — anything that culls by it must not conclude the group is nowhere.
Model liquids parse but are unused; the tileless single-height form was not seen in the sampled files.
Off-mesh connections are exercised by exactly one tile in the entire extraction (5622031.mmtile, Blade's Edge Arena, 2 connections).
Only 9 of 109 DBC stores are loaded
.map flight bounds are parsed past but discarded
Terrain holes are implemented but never exercised by a test against a known hole
World tables are imported by piping vendored .sql dumps — there is no real importer, no schema mapping and no type cleanup. 12 of upstream's 309 tables are vendored so far.
world structure is upstream's verbatim, not a schema we own. PLAN §5.2 wants cleaned types and names with columns and semantics preserved — that belongs in WowEmu.Data.Import.

remember: Session handlers that await resume on the tick, but nothing ENFORCES it: a future handler that writes ConfigureAwait(false) would silently resume on the thread pool and touch a Player from outside its loop. TickScheduler.AssertOwnerThread exists for exactly this and is not yet wired in.

THE TWO REFERENCE TREES ARE AT DIFFERENT POINTS IN AZEROTHCORE'S HISTORY, and creature spawning is the first place it bites. The C++ reads creature models from a creature_template_model table; the vendored database still has modelid1..4. Ours follows the DATA. Read the C++ for behaviour, but check the dump before trusting a column name.
Both reference trees (azerothcore-wotlk, database-wotlk) have no git root — updating means re-cloning.

sql/world/ is now ~19 MB, almost all of it creature (12 MB) and creature_template (7 MB). The vendoring rule says a fresh clone must be able to start, and that is the price. item_template will roughly double it.
data/ is 3 GB of extracted client data and is not committed; a fresh clone needs the extractors run again.
sql/world/ redistributes AGPL-3.0 content from AzerothCore's database. Deliberate — but it is a licence obligation worth being aware of.
conventions: Anything used from database-wotlk/ gets vendored into sql/world/ first, via tools/db/export-world.sh, with a note saying what reads it. The server never reads the reference checkout at runtime.
Extracted client data (data/) is the same idea in reverse: too large to commit, so it stays out and data/README.md records how to regenerate it.
Golden vectors and generated code are committed so that regenerating them is a visible diff.

vectors.note: Three sets, each generated by something other than our own code — a test that compares our C# against our C# proves nothing about protocol correctness. verify_vectors_in_tests.py checks that every generated value still appears in the test sources.

sets.by: generate_random_vectors.sh — SFMT + libstdc++ in a gcc container

why: AzerothCore does not roll its own distributions — it feeds SFMT into libstdc++'s uniform_int_distribution and uniform_real_distribution. Those consume a SPECIFIC number of 32-bit draws: the integer one rejection-samples, frand takes one and rand_norm takes two. An implementation that gets the draw count wrong still produces perfectly uniform numbers — and desynchronises the two servers' streams after the first roll.

The vectors are generated against libstdc++ specifically, inside a container, because libc++ (what clang uses on macOS) implements uniform_int_distribution differently. The generator has an #error guard so it cannot be built against the wrong standard library by accident.

ZEROCASE: SHA1Interleave skips leading zero bytes of the shared secret S. The obvious implementation is correct about 255 times out of 256 and fails whenever S happens to begin with a zero byte — an intermittent login failure that is very hard to trace. ZEROCASE is a handshake constructed so that S starts with 0x00, and a test asserts the correct answer genuinely differs from the naive one.

legal: This project reimplements a server for a game client it does not distribute. It contains no Blizzard assets. You must own a legitimate copy of the client, and all game data (.dbc, .map, .vmap, .mmap) is extracted locally and never committed.

vscode.note: Press ⌘⇧B to build, or ⌘⇧P → Tasks: Run Task for the rest.
